description: General amine acylation to an amide. Ordered graph reactants: nitrogen nucleophile; carbonyl donor whose leaving group is an acyclic O, Cl or S, or an imide-type N that carries a second carbonyl (for example an N-Boc amide). Plain amides, ureas and hydrazides are not donors, and lactones, lactams and cyclic anhydrides are excluded because the rule would delete the ring heteroatom; donor activation and amine compatibility are not constrained.
execution_caveats: Plain amides, ureas, hydrazides and ring-opening donors are excluded; donor activation (coupling reagent for acids) and amine compatibility are not constrained.
name: General amine acylation to an amide

reactant_roles.role: carbonyl donor with an acyclic O, Cl, S or imide N leaving group

description: N-substitution of an aromatic primary or secondary amine. Electrophile activation is not encoded; the carbon query includes aromatic carbon and the O/S alternatives need case-specific assessment.
execution_caveats: Electrophile activation is not encoded; the carbon query includes aromatic carbon and the O/S alternatives need case-specific assessment. Ring O/S leaving atoms are excluded.
name: N-substitution of an aromatic primary or secondary amine

reactant_roles.role: carbon electrophile bearing an acyclic Cl, Br, I, O or S leaving atom

description: O-linked carboxyl derivative reduction to alcohol. Ordered graph reactants: carbon-substituted acid, ester or anhydride with an acyclic leaving oxygen. The acyl O query does not distinguish acids from esters; carbonyl oxygen becomes the alcohol oxygen. Lactones are excluded because the rule would delete the ring oxygen.
execution_caveats: The acyl O query does not distinguish acids from esters; carbonyl oxygen becomes the alcohol oxygen. Lactones are excluded.
name: O-linked carboxyl derivative reduction to alcohol

reactant_roles.role: carbon-substituted acyl donor with an acyclic leaving oxygen

description: Mitsunobu substitution of a primary or secondary alcohol. Ordered graph reactants: primary or secondary alcohol that is not a hemiacetal; acidic O, N or S pronucleophile (carboxylic or phosphorus acid, phenol or heteroaryl hydroxyl, N-hydroxy compound, imide, sulfonamide, N-acyl hydroxylamine, hydrazoic acid, aromatic N-H heterocycle such as a tetrazole, triazole, imidazole, purine or pyridone, thiol or thioacid). The alcohol carbon is inverted. Basic amines, plain alcohols, aryl C-O bonds and ethers are not substrates.
execution_caveats: Azodicarboxylate and phosphine reagents are implicit and not grounded.
The alcohol carbon is inverted; an unspecified stereocenter stays unspecified.
Only the ring nitrogen drawn with the hydrogen reacts, so azole and purine regiochemistry follows the input tautomer; plain indoles and pyrroles are weak pronucleophiles.
Reverse simulation does not propose N-H heterocycle precursors; forward-simulate those instead.
name: Mitsunobu substitution of a primary or secondary alcohol with inversion

reactant_roles.role: acidic O, N or S pronucleophile

retro_planning_notes: Disconnect a C-O, C-N or C-S bond at a primary or secondary sp3 carbon to the alcohol with the opposite configuration and an acidic pronucleophile. Mitsunobu reagents are implicit.

description: Ether formation from an oxygen donor and carbon halide. Only O-H oxygens give valid products, and carboxylic acids give esters. The halide carbon may be alkyl, aryl, vinyl or acyl; aryl halides need activation or a copper or palladium catalyst that the rule does not encode.
execution_caveats: Carboxylic acids give esters; aryl halides need activation or a copper or palladium catalyst that the rule does not encode.
name: Ether formation from an oxygen donor and carbon halide

description: Carbonyl olefination with a phosphorus-bound carbon. Acid-derivative carbonyls (esters, amides, carbamates, acyl halides, thioesters) are excluded. No ylide charge or phosphonate activation is required by the query; not every C-P reagent is a usable olefination partner, and E/Z geometry is not encoded.
execution_caveats: No ylide charge or phosphonate activation is required by the query; not every C-P reagent is a usable olefination partner. E/Z geometry is not encoded.
name: Carbonyl olefination with a phosphorus-bound carbon

description: Broad chloride or bromide replacement by a heteroatom donor. The donor atom is written neutral in the product, so anionic donors such as iodide, azide or hydroxide salts give the neutral substitution product. Minimal donor and electrophile constraints allow chemically implausible matches; verify valence activation and product identity.
name: Broad chloride or bromide replacement by a heteroatom donor

reactant_roles.role: N O S P or I donor

description: N-carbamate cleavage to the parent nitrogen. The query includes multiple carbamate protecting groups without distinguishing their removal conditions; retained N has implicit hydrogen behavior. Cyclic carbamates such as oxazolidinones are excluded because the rule would delete ring atoms.
execution_caveats: The query includes multiple carbamate protecting groups without distinguishing their removal conditions; retained N has implicit hydrogen behavior. Cyclic carbamates are excluded.
name: N-carbamate cleavage to the parent nitrogen
